latest_findings.description: Browser history extraction (E-100) found no Chrome, Edge, or Firefox SQLite databases for the Administrator profile. Consistent with attacker using Internet Explorer (IE) on Windows Server 2008 — IE TypedURLs already recovered from NTUSER.DAT registry (phpMyAdmin, localhost, http://localhost/ at 2015-09-03 10:03:06 UTC). No Chromium-family browser was installed or used by the attacker on this host.
supporting_indicators: os_version: Windows Server 2008 — IE default browser

latest_findings.description: Registry file-access: surfaced 28 entries (lastvisitedpidlmru, opensavepidlmru, userassist). A file-access key proves a path was WRITTEN to a user-activity list, NOT that a human clicked it (background tasks populate UserAssist). LastWriteTimestamp = when the KEY changed, not when a value changed; corroborate with LNK / Jump Lists / ShellBags.

UserAssist confirms CompMgmtLauncher.exe (Computer Management) was GUI-launched at 2015-09-02 09:01:02 UTC — 5 seconds after the successful RDP logon (EVTX EID 4624 at 09:00:57). Run count 6. This directly corroborates the SAM finding (F-406): backdoor accounts user1 (09:05:06) and hacker (09:05:25) were created via Computer Management within 4 minutes of this launch. Three-source stack: UserAssist + SAM + EVTX EID 4624.
latest_findings.fk_confidence_note: FK multiplier 0.85 applied for registry_run. Original: 0.970 -> Adjusted: 0.825

latest_findings.description: UserAssist confirms cmd.exe (C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe) was GUI-launched at 2015-09-02 09:28:30 UTC — 28 minutes into the interactive RDP session. Run count 6. This corroborates the two active cmd.exe instances (PIDs 612, 1972) visible in memory and cmd.exe at ShimCache position 6. WordPad (Wordpad.lnk) was subsequently launched on 2015-09-03 07:20:06 UTC (Run count 6), followed 31 seconds later by the Open dialog selecting c99.php (OpenSavePidlMRU 07:20:37 UTC).

UserAssist confirms FTK Imager was launched from the VirtualBox shared folder (\\Vboxsvr\101\FTK-Imager\FTK Imager.exe) at 2015-09-03 10:03:37 UTC — 31 seconds after the VBoxsvr\101\Labs and FTK-Imager ShellBags were explored (10:03:04–10:03:32). FTK Imager was subsequently run from E:\FTK-Imager at 2015-09-12 18:19:47 UTC (forensic acquisition day per SAM last-login). The forensic examiner used FTK Imager transferred via the VirtualBox shared folder to acquire the memory and disk image evidence.

sigma_hunt (E-111) failed: path /cases/ALI-WEBSERVER-WIN-L0ZZQ76PMUF/artifacts/raw/evtx does not exist. Correct EVTX path confirmed at /mnt/disk/Windows/System32/winevt/Logs. Retrying sigma_hunt with correct path — mandatory Chainsaw rule-based detection not yet completed.

Chainsaw/Sigma hunt: 18 filtered rule hits across /mnt/disk/Windows/System32/winevt/Logs. Severity breakdown: {'informational': 18}. ATT&CK techniques detected: T1531. Full results at: /home/referenceensics/SAVVYDFIR-MCP/analysis/ALI-WEBSERVER-WIN-L0ZZQ76PMUF/sigma_hunt/chainsaw_20260606T132933Z.json

Chainsaw Sigma (2,284 rules) scanned 21 EVTX files and produced 18 hits — all informational severity, all matching the "User Logoff Event" rule (T1531/EID 4634) spanning 2015-08-23 to 2015-09-12. Zero detections at medium or above. No lateral movement, credential theft, PowerShell abuse, VSS deletion, scheduled task, or service-install patterns detected. This is consistent with the attacker operating exclusively via HTTP requests to PHP web shells (httpd.exe process), which generates no Windows-native process-creation events detectable by Sigma rules. The single failed logon (EID 4625) did not trigger a brute-force rule because only one failed attempt preceded success.
supporting_indicators: sigma_rule: User Logoff Event (T1531, count=18, 2015-08-23 to 2015-09-12)

latest_findings.description: Three independent sources (MFT, ShellBags, USN Journal) confirm web shell deployment at 2015-09-03T07:10–07:14 UTC: VBoxsvr shared-folder access preceded webshells.zip filesystem entry by 26 seconds, and Explorer shell state confirms the DVWA webshells directory was rendered immediately after deployment — proving VirtualBox host-to-guest transfer followed by web shell staging.
latest_findings.alternative_hypothesis: System administrator deployed web shell files for authorized DVWA security lab configuration or penetration test exercise.
evidence_against_it: Backdoor accounts user1 (RID 1005) and hacker (RID 1006) were created 22 hours before web shell deployment (SAM F-406), indicating unauthorized persistent access predated staging activity
phpshell2.php contained hardcoded reverse-connect payload targeting 192.168.56.102:4545 — attacker-controlled Meterpreter listener IP, not a lab infrastructure address
c99.php (153,275 bytes) is a full-featured attacker PHP web shell with file manager, command execution, and database access — inconsistent with authorized lab tooling

latest_findings.description: Two independent sources (EVTX EID 4624 Type 10 + UserAssist CompMgmtLauncher.exe) within 62 seconds confirm interactive RDP logon from 192.168.56.102 at 2015-09-02T09:00 UTC followed immediately by Computer Management launch, establishing the attacker account-creation sequence that produced backdoor accounts user1 and hacker within 5 minutes (corroborated by SAM hive F-406).
latest_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Legitimate administrator RDP-logged in and opened Computer Management for routine system maintenance, with user1/hacker accounts created as legitimate service accounts.
evidence_against_it: Account names 'hacker' and 'user1' have no legitimate enterprise naming convention; 'hacker' is not a standard service account name
Both accounts were added to Remote Desktop Users group — providing persistent external RDP access — which has no business justification for service accounts
Administrator failed logon at 09:00:39 UTC (SAM F-406) immediately before successful logon at 09:00:57 UTC suggests credential trial or brute-force, not routine admin activity

top_findings.description: Two independent sources (EVTX EID 4624 Type 10 + UserAssist CompMgmtLauncher.exe) within 62 seconds confirm interactive RDP logon from 192.168.56.102 at 2015-09-02T09:00 UTC followed immediately by Computer Management launch, establishing the attacker account-creation sequence that produced backdoor accounts user1 and hacker within 5 minutes (corroborated by SAM hive F-406).
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Legitimate administrator RDP-logged in and opened Computer Management for routine system maintenance, with user1/hacker accounts created as legitimate service accounts.
evidence_against_it: Account names 'hacker' and 'user1' have no legitimate enterprise naming convention; 'hacker' is not a standard service account name
Both accounts were added to Remote Desktop Users group — providing persistent external RDP access — which has no business justification for service accounts
Administrator failed logon at 09:00:39 UTC (SAM F-406) immediately before successful logon at 09:00:57 UTC suggests credential trial or brute-force, not routine admin activity
top_findings.fk_confidence_note: FK multiplier 0.85 applied for registry_run. Original: 0.900 -> Adjusted: 0.765

top_findings.description: Three independent sources (MFT, ShellBags, USN Journal) confirm web shell deployment at 2015-09-03T07:10–07:14 UTC: VBoxsvr shared-folder access preceded webshells.zip filesystem entry by 26 seconds, and Explorer shell state confirms the DVWA webshells directory was rendered immediately after deployment — proving VirtualBox host-to-guest transfer followed by web shell staging.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: System administrator deployed web shell files for authorized DVWA security lab configuration or penetration test exercise.
evidence_against_it: Backdoor accounts user1 (RID 1005) and hacker (RID 1006) were created 22 hours before web shell deployment (SAM F-406), indicating unauthorized persistent access predated staging activity
phpshell2.php contained hardcoded reverse-connect payload targeting 192.168.56.102:4545 — attacker-controlled Meterpreter listener IP, not a lab infrastructure address
c99.php (153,275 bytes) is a full-featured attacker PHP web shell with file manager, command execution, and database access — inconsistent with authorized lab tooling

top_findings.description: USN Journal corroborates web shell deployment chain: (1) 06:59:38 UTC — sqlmap temp PHP stubs tmpudvfh.php and tmpbrjvl.php deleted from htdocs (auto-cleanup); (2) 07:10:15 UTC — php3331.tmp created then renamed to phpshell.php in DVWA uploads (PHP file-upload temp→rename pattern, confirms HTTP POST delivery); (3) 07:14:51 UTC — c99.php and webshell.php extracted from webshells.zip then moved from webshells\ to DVWA root at 07:14:57; (4) 07:20:14–38 UTC — c99.php written to Administrator\AppData\Local\Temp (NotContentIndexed) then BOTH copies deleted within 24s; (5) 07:31:30 UTC — phpA4DB.tmp renamed to phpshell2.php in DVWA uploads (second Meterpreter shell upload). USN timestamps match MFT $SI values — no timestamp manipulation detected.

Chainsaw Sigma (2,284 rules) scanned 21 EVTX files and produced 18 hits — all informational severity, all matching the "User Logoff Event" rule (T1531/EID 4634) spanning 2015-08-23 to 2015-09-12. Zero detections at medium or above. No lateral movement, credential theft, PowerShell abuse, VSS deletion, scheduled task, or service-install patterns detected. This is consistent with the attacker operating exclusively via HTTP requests to PHP web shells (httpd.exe process), which generates no Windows-native process-creation events detectable by Sigma rules. The single failed logon (EID 4625) did not trigger a brute-force rule because only one failed attempt preceded success.
supporting_indicators: sigma_rule: User Logoff Event (T1531, count=18, 2015-08-23 to 2015-09-12)

top_findings.description: UserAssist confirms cmd.exe (C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe) was GUI-launched at 2015-09-02 09:28:30 UTC — 28 minutes into the interactive RDP session. Run count 6. This corroborates the two active cmd.exe instances (PIDs 612, 1972) visible in memory and cmd.exe at ShimCache position 6. WordPad (Wordpad.lnk) was subsequently launched on 2015-09-03 07:20:06 UTC (Run count 6), followed 31 seconds later by the Open dialog selecting c99.php (OpenSavePidlMRU 07:20:37 UTC).

OpenSavePidlMRU and LastVisitedPidlMRU registry keys confirm that c99.php (153KB full-featured web shell) was opened in WordPad.exe from C:\xampp\htdocs\DVWA\ at 2015-09-03 07:20:37 UTC. This proves interactive RDP-session access: the attacker used Windows Explorer file-open dialog to review or edit the web shell source directly on the victim server after deploying it via the upload vulnerability.

top_findings.description: Web shell phpshell.php (31 bytes) dropped in DVWA file upload directory at 2015-09-03 07:10:15 UTC via DVWA file upload vulnerability; webshells.zip (42,095 bytes) uploaded at 07:14:48 UTC with $SI Modified=2014-01-25 (M-before-B copy indicator — file originated from attacker system). Directory webshells\ extracted 3 seconds later at 07:14:51 UTC. phpshell2.php (945 bytes, Meterpreter reverse TCP shell) uploaded at 07:31:30 UTC. c99 (2).php (153,275 bytes, full-featured web shell) dropped in Administrator\AppData\Local\Temp at 07:20:14 UTC then DELETED (InUse=False).
No DKOM-hidden processes: pslist and psscan both enumerate 42 identical PIDs (psscan_only_count=0), ruling out DKOM rootkit process hiding on this host at time of acquisition.

ShellBags confirm the DVWA webshells directory (C:\xampp\htdocs\DVWA\webshells) was navigated at 2015-09-03 07:14:51 UTC — 3 seconds after webshells.zip was deployed (USN: 07:14:48). The attacker immediately browsed the directory after unzipping, verifying the deployed shells. The DVWA root was further explored at 07:20:31 UTC, immediately before c99.php was opened in WordPad (registry OpenSavePidlMRU: 07:20:37 UTC).

ShellBags show the VirtualBox shared folder (vboxsrv\Vboxsvr\101) was accessed at 2015-09-03 07:14:22 UTC — 26 seconds before webshells.zip was deployed per USN Journal (07:14:48). This proves webshells.zip was transferred from the attacker's host machine into the victim VM via the VirtualBox host-guest shared folder, not downloaded from the internet. VirtualBox shared 'Labs' and 'FTK-Imager' subfolders were also explored at 10:03:04–10:03:32 UTC, confirming sustained host-filesystem access.

UserAssist confirms FTK Imager was launched from the VirtualBox shared folder (\\Vboxsvr\101\FTK-Imager\FTK Imager.exe) at 2015-09-03 10:03:37 UTC — 31 seconds after the VBoxsvr\101\Labs and FTK-Imager ShellBags were explored (10:03:04–10:03:32). FTK Imager was subsequently run from E:\FTK-Imager at 2015-09-12 18:19:47 UTC (forensic acquisition day per SAM last-login). The forensic examiner used FTK Imager transferred via the VirtualBox shared folder to acquire the memory and disk image evidence.

ShellBags confirm the attacker interactively browsed DVWA vulnerability source code directories via RDP on 2015-09-02: \vulnerabilities\xss_r\source (11:36:25), \vulnerabilities\sqli\source (11:36:40), \vulnerabilities\upload\source (11:38:56). Viewing the upload vulnerability PHP source before exploiting it indicates deliberate reconnaissance of the attack surface from inside the server via the established RDP session.

IE TypedURLs registry key shows the attacker navigated to C:\xampp\phpMyAdmin locally (typed as a URL in IE address bar) at 2015-09-03 10:03:06 UTC, indicating local phpMyAdmin database access from the RDP session. Server Manager (ServerManager.msc) was also opened at 10:03:16 UTC. The Administrator account had a last-incorrect-password entry at 2015-09-02 09:00:39 UTC, matching the EVTX EID 4625 failed logon event, confirming the attacker probed the Administrator credential before a successful RDP logon at 09:00:57 UTC.
supporting_indicators: value_data: Administrator Last incorrect password: 2015-09-02 09:00:39 Last login: 2015-09-12 18:19:18

top_findings.description: Zero attacker-dropped PE executables appear in ShimCache for the Sep 2–3 2015 attack window. Attacker operated exclusively via PHP web shell interpreter (httpd.exe/PHP runtime), making the intrusion invisible to ShimCache execution tracking. This is a fileless web-layer attack pattern: all attacker commands executed within the Apache/PHP process, leaving no new .exe shimcache artifacts.

794 PHP session files (sess_*) created in xampp\tmp within 60 seconds on 2015-09-02 11:19:31–11:20:30 UTC — consistent with sqlmap automated SQL injection attack tool creating rapid session state. Sequential MFT entry numbers (62298–62326+) confirm simultaneous creation burst, not user activity.

EID 4625 (failed logon) at 2015-09-02 09:00:39 UTC targeting WIN-L0ZZQ76PMUF\Administrator LogonType 2 (console), immediately followed by EID 4624 (successful logon) at 09:00:57 UTC LogonType 2 (interactive console) targeting Administrator — 18-second gap indicates password correction or retry after fat-finger. Also EID 4625 at 06:00:41 targeting WIN-L0ZZQ76PMUF\Guest via LogonType 3 (network) with user restriction failure — attacker probing network-accessible guest account. All RemoteHost fields show 127.0.0.1 or local — no external RDP IP captured in Security log; TerminalServices log not extracted.

SAM hive confirms two backdoor local accounts created during the intrusion: 'user1' (RID 1005, created 2015-09-02 09:05:06 UTC) and 'hacker' (RID 1006, created 2015-09-02 09:05:25 UTC). Both accounts were added to the Remote Desktop Users group, establishing persistent RDP access. Neither account shows a last-login timestamp, indicating they were created for future use and not yet actively used via RDP. SAM LastWriteTimestamp 2015-09-02 09:05:25 UTC.
supporting_indicators: value_data: Username: user1 Id: 1005 Created: 2015-09-02 09:05:06 Account flags: NormalUserAccount
value_data: Username: hacker Id: 1006 Created: 2015-09-02 09:05:25 Account flags: NormalUserAccount

top_findings.description: LNK file extraction (E-093) returned zero rows for the Administrator profile despite ShellBags confirming Explorer navigation to DVWA, webshells, and XAMPP directories. Absence of LNK shortcuts in %AppData%\Recent while ShellBags show active GUI navigation indicates the Recent folder was cleared (anti-forensics) or all file access was performed via browser/command-line without triggering LNK creation. ShellBags+OpenSavePidlMRU remain the primary file-reference artifacts for this session.
supporting_indicators: artifact_absent: LNK files (zero rows, Administrator profile)
shellbags_present: DVWA, webshells, XAMPP navigation confirmed
anti_forensics_indicator: Recent folder cleared or bypassed
